sections.text: The size barely changes the price, so buy the size your wall needs

sections.content: This is the most useful thing on the page. The [3D Islamic Allah clock](/product/3d-islamic-wooden-wall-clock-with-allah-design-elegant-decorative-clock-for-home) is 16 inches and costs Rs. 1,050. The [3D world map clock](/product/3d-wooden-world-map-with-esthetic-dial-wall-clock-best-quality-wall-clock-for-ho) is 40 inches and costs Rs. 1,151. That is 10% more money for roughly six times the surface area.

So there is no cheaper-per-inch logic to reward. The cheapest clock we sell is Rs. 804 and the dearest is Rs. 1,218 — a 51% gap across the whole catalogue, which is smaller than the gap between two brands of the same shirt. Pick the design and the size you want. The budget is not going to be the problem.

sections.text: Quartz, silent, and the part nobody asks about

sections.content: Almost nobody asks what movement is inside a wall clock, which is odd, because the movement is the only part that actually tells the time. Ours are standard quartz — the same mechanism as a Rs. 15,000 branded clock on a shelf in a showroom.

A quartz movement is accurate to about a second a day, which drifts by a few minutes a year. That is a real limitation, and [the quartz clock explainer on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz_clock) covers the mechanism if you want the detail. If you want to know what time it officially is, [time.gov](https://www.time.gov/) is run by the US standards bodies and is never wrong. A decorative clock is not a stopwatch, and it is not pretending to be.
One thing worth knowing: the Islamic calligraphy clocks have an optional LED-lit version. If you want the backlit one, say so on WhatsApp, because it is not a separate product listing.

sections.text: Don't buy a wall clock from us if…

sections.content: You want an heirloom. These are Rs. 800 to Rs. 1,200 decorative clocks made from 3mm lasani wood. They are light, they look good on a wall, and they will not be worth more in twenty years. If you are after something to pass down, a jeweller is the right shop and we are not.

You need it tomorrow. Our delivery is 2-4 working days, and no amount of WhatsApp urgency changes what a courier does. If a birthday starts in five hours, go to the physical bazaar and we will see you for the next one.

You have not measured the wall. A 40-inch map clock is genuinely large. Hold a tape measure against the space first — it takes thirty seconds now and saves a return later. You can read [our free delivery terms](/blog/online-shopping-free-delivery-pakistan) while you are deciding, and [how cash on delivery works](/blog/cash-on-delivery-pakistan-online-shopping) if you would rather not pay upfront.

Twelve clocks, four honest use cases. The Islamic calligraphy designs — Inna Allaha, the Allah design, Loh-e-Qurani and Qul Naas — suit a drawing room, a study or a mosque, and they are the ones people buy as gifts. At Rs. 943 to Rs. 1,134 they are also the easiest gift to get right, because nobody has to guess a size before they wrap it.

The world map and the tile clock are the modern pair. The map is 40 inches, which is genuinely large and needs a wall that can spare it. The [3D tile wall clock](/product/3d-tile-wall-clock-wooden-tile-wall-clock-frame-wall-art-wall-decoration-decor-f) comes in 20 or 30 inches and is the one we sell most, so it evidently lands in the middle of most rooms.

For a child's room, the butterfly at Rs. 804 and the forest deer at Rs. 1,151 are the obvious picks. The butterfly is the cheapest thing we sell in this category, and it is still a laser-cut 3D piece rather than a printed face. The plainest option is the 3D DIY MDF clock at Rs. 1,218 — it is the quietest of the twelve, which is usually what a room you work in actually wants.

items.q: What is the price of a wall clock in Pakistan?
items.a: At BazaarNow, wall clocks run from Rs. 804 to Rs. 1,218 as of October 2026, with twelve designs in stock. Free delivery is included across Pakistan.

items.q: Do you deliver wall clocks across Pakistan?
items.a: Yes. Delivery takes 2-4 working days to every major city, from Lahore and Karachi to Gilgit and Skardu. Delivery is free on all orders.

items.q: Can I pay cash on delivery for a wall clock?
items.a: Yes, on every order, and you can inspect the clock before you pay. Paying in advance by JazzCash, EasyPaisa or bank transfer takes a further 5% off instead.

items.q: What sizes do your wall clocks come in?
items.a: The sizes we can confirm are 16, 20, 25, 30 and 40 inches. Some designs do not have a stated size yet, so message us on WhatsApp and we will measure the specific piece before you order.
They use quartz movements, which tick rather than chime. The MDF quartz clock is the quietest of the twelve. None of them chime hourly, so none will wake anyone up.

items.q: Do the Islamic calligraphy clocks come with LED lights?
items.a: Some designs have an optional LED-lit version, including the Inna Allaha clock. It is not listed as a separate product, so ask on WhatsApp before ordering if you want the lit one.

sections.content: A wall clock is the rare purchase where the cheapest one and the dearest one do the same job, and the only real decision is which wall it goes on. Measure the wall, pick the design, and let us handle the rest — free delivery, cash on delivery, and a 7-day window if the 40-inch one turns out to be a 40-inch one.
